headline: Congress cancels a federal rule that would have limited overdraft fees at very large banks and credit unions.
what_it_does: This law cancels a Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule published on December 30, 2024. That rule would have required very large financial institutions to cap overdraft fees at $5, set a higher cap they could justify, or treat overdrafts as loans under Truth in Lending Act disclosure rules. With the rule canceled, those requirements do not take effect.

who_it_affects.group: Customers of very large banks and credit unions who overdraw their accounts
who_it_affects.how: Their overdraft fees will not be subject to the $5 cap or the other limits the canceled rule would have set.
They do not have to change how they charge for overdrafts or follow the loan disclosure rules the canceled rule would have required.
Its overdraft rule for very large institutions is voided, and under the Congressional Review Act it generally cannot issue a substantially similar rule without new approval from Congress.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted May 9, 2025; the rule is nullified as of enactment.
